exposure: High-risk delivery factors (prolonged second stage of labour, foetal heart rate deceleration or acceleration, emergency caesarean section, placental insufficiency)
cohort: The study included 100 term neonates born at a single hospital to mothers who experienced high-risk delivery factors such as prolonged second stage of labour, foetal heart rate issues, emergency caesarean section, or placental insufficiency.
finding: High-risk term babies with cord pH <7.25 showed an increased need for resuscitation, NICU admission, and delay in achieving full feeds compared to those with pH >7.25, though no statistical correlation was found between cord blood pH and the incidence of convulsions or encephalopathy.
